solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Seat in a horrid WC's wobbly

indicators.note: something wobbly is unsteady and out of shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone sits on a shaky seat in a nasty lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link word but is part of the fodder: IN A HORRID WCS has the twelve letters needed.
explanation.definitionFit: A Windsor chair is a type of wooden chair with a spindle back, so it is a kind of seat.

clue.text: I cleared out, giving accommodation to north countryman

indicators.note: giving accommodation to means housing, so the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside them
out signals that the letters of the words before it are disordered, put out of place

explanation.surface: Someone clears out to make room for a man from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges I CLEARED into ICELADER; 'giving accommodation to' puts N inside it. 'north' seems to describe the countryman but only supplies N, though Iceland is indeed northern.
explanation.definitionFit: An Icelander is a native of Iceland, a man from that country, hence a countryman.

clue.text: Drive onto part of ship? That's the plan

parts.note: Dr is the usual abbreviation for Drive in street names
aft is the rear part of a ship

explanation.surface: Driving on to a ship's deck is the scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: DR for Drive, as on a street sign, then AFT, the stern end of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft is a preliminary version or outline, a plan to be worked up later.

clue.text: Order Paper is presented to House, ultimately

parts.note: an organ is a newspaper or journal speaking for a group

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word house

explanation.surface: An Order Paper, the parliamentary agenda, is presented to the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order Paper' reads as one parliamentary term, but splits: Order is the definition and Paper gives ORGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To order things is to arrange them methodically, a synonym for putting them in shape.

clue.text: Ill-tempered councillor bouncing baby

indicators.note: bouncing jumbles the letters of the following word like a jiggled infant

explanation.surface: A grumpy local councillor bounces a baby on the knee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bouncing' seems to describe a lively infant on a knee, but it is the anagram signal for the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Crabby means irritable and bad-tempered, like a cross, snappy person.

clue.text: Bottom in algebra? For revision turns to a high-flier

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom of a word is its final letter, here of algebra
for revision means to be revised, so the letters gathered are reworked

explanation.surface: A student hits rock bottom in algebra and goes off to revise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom' sounds like a poor mark, but is the last letter A of algebra; with TURNS TO A it is rearranged by 'For revision'.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronaut travels into space, literally flying higher than anyone, a punning take on a high achiever.

clue.text: Old-fashioned postal worker, demanding rise, hasn't succeeded

indicators.note: succeeded is abbreviated S, and hasn't means that letter is dropped
in a down clue a rise reads the word upwards, so it is turned back to front

parts.note: a sorter separates mail at a sorting office

explanation.surface: A traditional postman demands a pay rise but fails to get it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'demanding rise' turns SORTER into RETROS, and 'hasn't succeeded' takes off its S.
explanation.definitionFit: Retro describes styles imitating or revived from the past, so it means old-fashioned.

clue.text: True-sounding professional detective needing time to safeguard what's on computer?

indicators.note: sounding says the word for true is to be taken as it is pronounced, giving a different spelling

parts.note: true means correct, right
pro is short for professional
tec is slang shortening of detective

explanation.surface: A genuine private eye needs time to guard computer files.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' turns RIGHT (true) into its soundalike WRITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting write-protection on a disk or file stops data being changed, a way of guarding stored material.

clue.text: Bandleader fell over, grabbing woman

indicators.note: over means the caught letters are turned head over heels, read backwards
grabbing means the two words hold the letters wanted, caught within them

explanation.surface: A bandleader tumbles and clutches at a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of bandleADER and the F of Fell give ADERF, which 'over' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Freda is a female first name, so it fits a clue asking for a woman.

clue.text: Unlikely to be summoned to court? That's priceless!

definitions.text: Unlikely to be summoned to court?
definitions.meaning: someone with no accusation against them faces no court summons

explanation.definitionFit: Free of charge means costing nothing, and read literally means not facing a criminal accusation.

clue.text: Starting to circulate around a heavenly body

indicators.note: around means the shuffled letters surround the next piece
to circulate means to move round, so the letters of the first word are shuffled

explanation.surface: Something begins to orbit a celestial object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to circulate' rearranges STARTING and 'around' wraps it round A.
explanation.definitionFit: A giant star is a large, luminous star, one kind of heavenly body.

clue.text: Protein in eggs and beer? The reverse

indicators.note: the reverse says the words just built are to be read the other way round

parts.note: nits are the eggs of lice
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether eggs and beer contain protein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The reverse' seems to suggest swapping 'beer' and 'eggs', but it reverses the letters of NITSALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastin is an elastic protein found in skin and connective tissue.

clue.text: Withdraw after eating large feast

indicators.note: after eating means once the phrase has swallowed the next piece inside it

parts.note: to bow out is to withdraw or retire
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone leaves the table after a huge meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A blowout is informal for a lavish meal or big celebration.

clue.text: Ancient language, one lords misused

indicators.note: misused means wrongly handled, so the letters are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A tongue from long ago that one aristocrat abused.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Norse is the medieval Scandinavian tongue of the Vikings.

clue.text: Old writer inspired by Calliope and Erato, say, will produce volumes

indicators.note: inspired means breathed in, so the pen point goes inside the goddesses

parts.note: Calliope and Erato are two of the nine Muses, and say marks them as examples
a nib is the writing point of a pen

explanation.surface: An ancient author, inspired by the Muses of poetry, will write books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspired by' suggests artistic inspiration, but literally means breathed in, i.e. contained. Calliope (epic poetry) and Erato (love poetry) are two of the nine Muses.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnibus is a single volume collecting several works, so the plural is volumes.

clue.text: Put in prison, outlaw wants dog returned

parts.note: to outlaw something is to ban it

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the word for the dog is read backwards

parts.note: a pug is a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: A jailed outlaw wants his dog given back.
explanation.definitionFit: To bang up is British slang for locking someone in a cell.

clue.text: Shock as vehicle is caught in heavy wind

indicators.note: caught in means trapped within, so the vehicle pieces sit inside the wind

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A shock as a van is caught in a storm.
explanation.definitionFit: To galvanise is to jolt someone into action, as with an electric charge.

clue.text: Think about Tory party dominating right

indicators.note: dominating means standing over, which in a down clue puts these pieces above the next

parts.note: Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party
a side is a party in a dispute or game

explanation.surface: Consider a Conservative party lording it over the right wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dominating' places CONSIDE above R in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To consider is to think carefully about something, to weigh it.

clue.text: French soldier captured in Crecy ran off

indicators.note: captured in means held prisoner within the following words

explanation.surface: A French soldier taken at the battle of Crecy fled.
explanation.walkthrough: Crecy was a 1346 battle between England and France, apt for a French soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyrano de Bergerac was a seventeenth-century French soldier and writer, hero of Rostand's play.

clue.text: Music maker introducing really big-time comic, formerly

indicators.note: introducing means bringing in, so the inserted pieces go inside the instrument

parts.note: a cello is a stringed instrument that makes music
OS stands for outsize, a clothing size for really big

explanation.surface: A musician introduces a hugely successful comedian of the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big-time' looks like one word but splits: really big gives OS and time gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: Lou Costello was half of the American comedy double act Abbott and Costello, a comedian of decades past.

clue.text: Soldiers confronting wicked threat

parts.note: men are soldiers, as in officers and men
wicked is slang for excellent, as is ace

explanation.surface: Soldiers face down a sinister danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wicked' looks sinister but is slang praise, meaning ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A menace is a danger or threat to someone.

clue.text: Good-natured fellow features in a story

indicators.note: features in means appears inside, so the letter for fellow goes within the story

parts.note: a fable is a short moral story

explanation.surface: A kindly chap appears in a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable means friendly and easy to talk to, pleasant in manner.

clue.text: Swindle woman from Bonn, Germany

parts.note: Frau is the German word for a woman or wife, and Bonn is a German city
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A German woman pulls off a con.
explanation.definitionFit: A fraud is a deception or con carried out for gain.

clue.text: Rescue fifty held captive by brute

indicators.note: held captive by means trapped inside, so the numeral goes within the brute

parts.note: a savage is a brutal, uncivilised person
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Fifty hostages held by a monster need saving.
explanation.definitionFit: To salvage something is to save it from loss or wreckage.

clue.text: A person avoiding alcohol is into the French style of coffee

indicators.note: is into means goes inside, so these pieces sit within the French article

parts.note: le is French for the
TT stands for teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: A teetotaller is keen on French-style coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is into' looks like 'is keen on' but means placed inside LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A latte is espresso with a lot of steamed milk, one way coffee is served.

clue.text: Animal seen by lake in splendid grazing area

indicators.note: in puts the animal and lake inside the word for splendid

parts.note: grand means splendid or magnificent

indicators.note: seen by means placed beside, so the lake letter follows the animal

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, an animal
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A donkey grazes beside a lake in a lovely meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Grassland is open land covered with grass, used by animals for grazing.

clue.text: Oliver? Leading parts in that would interest some thespians

definitions.note: Oliver is the orphan hero of Dickens's novel, and the question mark flags a definition by example

indicators.note: leading parts are the front letters of each of the following words

explanation.surface: The lead roles in the musical Oliver! would appeal to actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading parts' looks like starring roles for actors but takes the first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist is the title character of Dickens's novel, so his surname is clued by his first name.

clue.text: Put off food consumed about mid-afternoon with newspaper chief

parts.note: a dish is food prepared for a meal

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for consumed wraps the next letter

parts.note: eaten means consumed

indicators.note: mid points to the central letter of the word afternoon

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the chief of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A meal eaten around mid-afternoon with an editor puts someone off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts R, the middle letter from 'mid-afternoon', inside EATEN to make EARTEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To be disheartened is to be discouraged, having lost heart or enthusiasm.
